_meta.indication: Treatment of patients with locally advanced or metastatic urothelial carcinoma who have disease progression during or following platinum-containing chemotherapy, or within 12 months of neoadjuvant or adjuvant platinum-containing chemotherapy; approved under accelerated approval based on tumor response rate and duration of response

pivotal_trials.nct: Not stated in reviewed documents for Study 1108 (the confirmatory Phase III trial is NCT02516241)
pivotal_trials.design: Single-arm, open-label, multicenter, dose-escalation/exploration and dose-expansion study; efficacy assessed in the UBC cohort
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with locally advanced or metastatic urothelial carcinoma who progressed during or after a platinum-based therapy, including within 12 months of neoadjuvant or adjuvant therapy
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Confirmed Objective Response Rate (ORR) per RECIST v1.1 by Blinded Independent Central Review (BICR), and duration of response (DoR)
pivotal_trials.result: ORR by BICR 17.0% (95% CI 11.9, 23.3) in all 182 patients (5 complete responses, 26 partial responses); ORR 26.3% in PD-L1 high (N=95) and 4.1% in PD-L1 low/negative (N=73); median DoR not reached in all patients

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥15%) were fatigue (39%), musculoskeletal pain (24%), constipation (21%), decreased appetite (19%), nausea (16%), peripheral edema (15%) and urinary tract infection (15%). Serious risks are immune-mediated pneumonitis, hepatitis, colitis, endocrinopathies, nephritis, and infection.
target_moa: Human IgG1 kappa monoclonal antibody that blocks the interaction of PD-L1 with PD-1 and CD80 (B7.1), releasing inhibition of immune responses
companion_dx_detail: PD-L1 expression was evaluated with the VENTANA PD-L1 (SP263) Assay for a subgroup analysis, but the indication is not restricted by PD-L1 status; no companion diagnostic requirement

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee convened; the application was not referred to the Oncologic Drugs Advisory Committee

description.text: Added new indication for unresectable Stage III NSCLC not progressed after concurrent platinum-based chemoradiation

description.text: Updated overall survival data for the PACIFIC trial and modified the Immunogenicity section; no new indication or population added

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental biologics application provides for updates to the overall survival data for the PACIFIC trial (14.2) and modifications to the Adverse Reactions, Immunogenicity (6.2) section of the package insert to remove the statement regarding assay performance and clarify the source of the data for immunogenicity. This sBLA also contained the final study report for PMC 3329-01 cited in our approval letter for sBLA 760169/S-002, issued February 16, 2018. Finally, this sBLA relied on previously submitted data contained in your June 29, 2018, amendment containing the final study report for PMC 3205-05 cited in our approval letter for BLA 761069, issued May 1, 2017, in support of your proposed labeling changes to Section 6.2 of the package insert.

surrogate_endpoint.text: Tumor response rate (ORR) and duration of response, considered reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit

citations.quote: This indication is approved under accelerated approval based on tumor response rate and duration of response. Continued approval for this indication may be contingent upon verification and description of clinical benefit in confirmatory trials [see *Clinical Studies (14.1)*].

Overall, the improvement in the surrogates, objective response rate (ORR) and duration of response (DOR), is reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit for the use of durvalumab in the intended patient population.

summary.text: Durvalumab received Breakthrough Therapy Designation (February 2016) and Priority Review, and was granted accelerated approval under Subpart E based on ORR and duration of response from the single-arm Study 1108 UBC cohort, with a required confirmatory Phase III randomized trial (NCT02516241) to verify clinical benefit.

citations.quote: Breakthrough Designation was granted in February 2016 for the treatment of pts with PD-L1 positive metastatic or locally advanced urothelial bladder cancer whose tumor has progressed during or after 1 platinum-based regimen.
Priority or Standard	Priority Review
The clinical and statistical reviewers recommend accelerated approval of durvalumab for the proposed indication under Subpart E of the Biological Licensing Regulations1.

An ongoing randomized, active controlled trial of durvalumab versus durvalumab in combination with the CTLA-4 antagonist tremelimumab versus the Investigator's choice of chemotherapeutic may provide confirmatory evidence (NCT02516241).
